title: Switch to using a texture for global shader parameters in the Compatibility renderer
body:
Proper solution for: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/85374 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/91836 (the previous solution helped avoid the spurious error. But it didn't solve the core of the problem

Fixes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/114949
Fixes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/112674
Fixes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/108151
Should fix (but not sure since I can't repro): https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/122741

This allows us to overcome the small limit for UBO size on some platforms. The fundamental problem is that OpenGL only guarantees a max UBO size of at least 16384 bytes. For the global shader params, that is fine. But we reuse the same buffer for instance shader parameters. Each node using an instance shader param takes 16 slots from the buffer. Each slot is 4 floats, so it takes 16 bytes. Therefore, each node takes 256 bytes from the buffer. If your device only supports 16384 bytes, then you can only have 64 nodes with per-instance data! Most desktop devices however support 65536 bytes, so they can have a whopping **256 nodes** using per-instance data. 

Being limited to 256 nodes really defeats the purpose of having instance shader params in the first place. So we need to switch to a different data storage format. The only other thing available is textures. Which is what this PR switches to. 

Also note, the default value for `rendering/limits/global_shader_variables/buffer_size` is `65536` which was basically never supported in the compatibility renderer. Now it can be increased as high as 1048576 before even the weakest devices start to hit hardware limits.

In theory, this may be slightly slower on some platforms since the OpenGL spec says that UBO access should always be at least as fast as texture access (and may be faster).

In practice it should not matter. On Adreno devices for example, texture fetches are faster than UBO fetches, but only when the sum of all UBOs in the shader are less than 7,372 bytes. Since the global shader UBO was 16384 bytes by default, we blew pasty that limit. So this should result in the same or better performance on Adreno devices.

Overall, its a correctness change. So performance is only a factor if it results in a significant reduction.

Testing locally on a linux machine with an iGPU, there is no measurable performance change at 1024 nodes (the max supported by this device and most devices before this PR).
